paper_metadata.title: OsCo-based high-temperature bulk metallic glasses with robust mechanical properties

evidence.quote: A family of novel Os–Co–Ta–B high-temperature bulk metallic glasses (HTBMGs) was fabricated by introducing high-modulus refractory metal Os (50 wt% at least) and strong-covalent metalloid B (up to 40 at%).

The corresponding mixtures of Os, Co, and B were firstly alloyed by induction melting in a high-purity argon atmosphere to prevent the splashing loss of B.
Then, the prealloys and the remained Ta were remelted four times by arc-melting in a Ti-gettered pure argon atmosphere to ensure the chemical homogeneity.
Cylindrical samples with different diameters were prepared by copper mold casting.

The yield strength (σy) decreases gradually accompanied by the increase of plastic deformation in the ambient temperature, and remains 4.1 GPa (over 60% room-temperature strength) even at 0.85 Tg (873 K).
The impressive strength is attributed to the strong bond characteristics especially for Ta–Os and B–B bonds.
The introduction of Os element substantially increases the Young’s modulus by ~20 GPa compared with that of the Co–Ta–B ternary BMGs with the similar composition.
